     6	
     7	# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis
     8	
     9	## Overview
    10	
    11	A .docx file is a ZIP archive containing XML files.
    12	
    13	## Quick Reference
    14	
    15	| Task | Approach |
    16	|------|----------|
    17	| Read/analyze content | `pandoc` or unpack for raw XML |
    18	| Create new document | Use `docx-js` - see Creating New Documents below |
    19	| Edit existing document | Unpack → edit XML → repack - see Editing Existing Documents below |
    20	
    21	### Converting .doc to .docx
    22	
    23	Legacy `.doc` files must be converted before editing:
    24	
    25	```bash
    26	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx document.doc
    27	```
    28	
    29	### Reading Content
    30	
    31	```bash
    32	# Text extraction with tracked changes
    33	pandoc --track-changes=all document.docx -o output.md
    34	
    35	# Raw XML access
    36	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
    37	```
    38	
    39	### Converting to Images
    40	
    41	```bash
    42	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf document.docx
    43	pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 document.pdf page
    44	```
    45	
    46	### Accepting Tracked Changes
    47	
    48	To produce a clean document with all tracked changes accepted (requires LibreOffice):
    49	
    50	```bash
    51	python scripts/accept_changes.py input.docx output.docx
    52	```
    53	
    54	---
    55	
    56	## Creating New Documents
    57	
    58	Generate .docx files with JavaScript, then validate. Install: `npm install -g docx`
    59	
    60	### Setup
    61	```javascript
    62	const { Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, Table, TableRow, TableCell, ImageRun,
    63	        Header, Footer, AlignmentType, PageOrientation, LevelFormat, ExternalHyperlink,
    64	        InternalHyperlink, Bookmark, FootnoteReferenceRun, PositionalTab,
    65	        PositionalTabAlignment, PositionalTabRelativeTo, PositionalTabLeader,
    66	        TabStopType, TabStopPosition, Column, SectionType,
    67	        TableOfContents, HeadingLevel, BorderStyle, WidthType, ShadingType,
    68	        VerticalAlign, PageNumber, PageBreak } = require('docx');
    69	
    70	const doc = new Document({ sections: [{ children: [/* content */] }] });
    71	Packer.toBuffer(doc).then(buffer => fs.writeFileSync("doc.docx", buffer));
    72	```
    73	
    74	### Validation
    75	After creating the file, validate it. If validation fails, unpack, fix the XML, and repack.
    76	```bash
    77	python scripts/office/validate.py doc.docx
    78	```
    79	
    80	### Page Size
    81	
    82	```javascript
    83	// CRITICAL: docx-js defaults to A4, not US Letter
    84	// Always set page size explicitly for consistent results
    85	sections: [{
    86	  properties: {
    87	    page: {
    88	      size: {
    89	        width: 12240,   // 8.5 inches in DXA
    90	        height: 15840   // 11 inches in DXA
    91	      },
    92	      margin: { top: 1440, right: 1440, bottom: 1440, left: 1440 } // 1 inch margins
    93	    }
    94	  },
    95	  children: [/* content */]
    96	}]
    97	```
    98	
    99	**Common page sizes (DXA units, 1440 DXA = 1 inch):**
   100	
   101	| Paper | Width | Height | Content Width (1" margins) |
   102	|-------|-------|--------|---------------------------|
   103	| US Letter | 12,240 | 15,840 | 9,360 |
   104	| A4 (default) | 11,906 | 16,838 | 9,026 |
   105	
   106	**Landscape orientation:** docx-js swaps width/height internally, so pass portrait dimensions and let it handle the swap:
   107	```javascript
   108	size: {
   109	  width: 12240,   // Pass SHORT edge as width
   110	  height: 15840,  // Pass LONG edge as height
   111	  orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE  // docx-js swaps them in the XML
   112	},
   113	// Content width = 15840 - left margin - right margin (uses the long edge)
   114	```
   115	
   116	### Styles (Override Built-in Headings)
   117	
   118	Use Arial as the default font (universally supported). Keep titles black for readability.
   119	
   120	```javascript
   121	const doc = new Document({
   122	  styles: {
   123	    default: { document: { run: { font: "Arial", size: 24 } } }, // 12pt default
   124	    paragraphStyles: [
   125	      // IMPORTANT: Use exact IDs to override built-in styles
   126	      { id: "Heading1", name: "Heading 1", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   127	        run: { size: 32, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   128	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 240, after: 240 }, outlineLevel: 0 } }, // outlineLevel required for TOC
   129	      { id: "Heading2", name: "Heading 2", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,
   130	        run: { size: 28, bold: true, font: "Arial" },
   131	        paragraph: { spacing: { before: 180, after: 180 }, outlineLevel: 1 } },
   132	    ]
   133	  },
   134	  sections: [{
   135	    children: [
   136	      new Paragraph({ heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, children: [new TextRun("Title")] }),
   137	    ]
   138	  }]
   139	});
   140	```
   141	
   142	### Lists (NEVER use unicode bullets)
   143	
   144	```javascript
   145	// ❌ WRONG - never manually insert bullet characters
   146	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("• Item")] })  // BAD
   147	new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("\u2022 Item")] })  // BAD
   148	
   149	// ✅ CORRECT - use numbering config with LevelFormat.BULLET
   150	const doc = new Document({
   151	  numbering: {
   152	    config: [
   153	      { reference: "bullets",
   154	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.BULLET, text: "•", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   155	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },
   156	      { reference: "numbers",
   157	        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.DECIMAL, text: "%1.", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,
   158	          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },
   159	    ]
   160	  },
   161	  sections: [{
   162	    children: [
   163	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "bullets", level: 0 },
   164	        children: [new TextRun("Bullet item")] }),
   165	      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: "numbers", level: 0 },
   166	        children: [new TextRun("Numbered item")] }),
   167	    ]
   168	  }]
   169	});
   170	
   171	// ⚠️ Each reference creates INDEPENDENT numbering
   172	// Same reference = continues (1,2,3 then 4,5,6)
   173	// Different reference = restarts (1,2,3 then 1,2,3)
   174	```
   175	
   176	### Tables
   177	
   178	**CRITICAL: Tables need dual widths** - set both `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on each cell. Without both, tables render incorrectly on some platforms.
   179	
   180	```javascript
   181	// CRITICAL: Always set table width for consistent rendering
   182	// CRITICAL: Use ShadingType.CLEAR (not SOLID) to prevent black backgrounds
   183	const border = { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 1, color: "CCCCCC" };
   184	const borders = { top: border, bottom: border, left: border, right: border };
   185	
   186	new Table({
   187	  width: { size: 9360, type: WidthType.DXA }, // Always use DXA (percentages break in Google Docs)
   188	  columnWidths: [4680, 4680], // Must sum to table width (DXA: 1440 = 1 inch)
   189	  rows: [
   190	    new TableRow({
   191	      children: [
   192	        new TableCell({
   193	          borders,
   194	          width: { size: 4680, type: WidthType.DXA }, // Also set on each cell
   195	          shading: { fill: "D5E8F0", type: ShadingType.CLEAR }, // CLEAR not SOLID
   196	          margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }, // Cell padding (internal, not added to width)
   197	          children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun("Cell")] })]
   198	        })
   199	      ]
   200	    })
   201	  ]
   202	})
   203	```
   204	
   205	**Table width calculation:**
   206	
   207	Always use `WidthType.DXA` — `WidthType.PERCENTAGE` breaks in Google Docs.
   208	
   209	```javascript
   210	// Table width = sum of columnWidths = content width
   211	// US Letter with 1" margins: 12240 - 2880 = 9360 DXA
   212	width: { size: 9360, type: WidthType.DXA },
   213	columnWidths: [7000, 2360]  // Must sum to table width
   214	```
   215	
   216	**Width rules:**
	< truncated lines 217-374 >
   375	}]
   376	```
   377	
   378	### Critical Rules for docx-js
   379	
   380	- **Set page size explicitly** - docx-js defaults to A4; use US Letter (12240 x 15840 DXA) for US documents
   381	- **Landscape: pass portrait dimensions** - docx-js swaps width/height internally; pass short edge as `width`, long edge as `height`, and set `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE`
   382	- **Never use `\n`** - use separate Paragraph elements
   383	- **Never use unicode bullets** - use `LevelFormat.BULLET` with numbering config
   384	- **PageBreak must be in Paragraph** - standalone creates invalid XML
   385	- **ImageRun requires `type`** - always specify png/jpg/etc
   386	- **Always set table `width` with DXA** - never use `WidthType.PERCENTAGE` (breaks in Google Docs)
   387	- **Tables need dual widths** - `columnWidths` array AND cell `width`, both must match
   388	- **Table width = sum of columnWidths** - for DXA, ensure they add up exactly
   389	- **Always add cell margins** - use `margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }` for readable padding
   390	- **Use `ShadingType.CLEAR`** - never SOLID for table shading
   391	- **Never use tables as dividers/rules** - cells have minimum height and render as empty boxes (including in headers/footers); use `border: { bottom: { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 6, color: "2E75B6", space: 1 } }` on a Paragraph instead. For two-column footers, use tab stops (see Tab Stops section), not tables
   392	- **TOC requires HeadingLevel only** - no custom styles on heading paragraphs
   393	- **Override built-in styles** - use exact IDs: "Heading1", "Heading2", etc.
   394	- **Include `outlineLevel`** - required for TOC (0 for H1, 1 for H2, etc.)
   395	
   396	---
   397	
   398	## Editing Existing Documents
   399	
   400	**Follow all 3 steps in order.**
   401	
   402	### Step 1: Unpack
   403	```bash
   404	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
   405	```
   406	Extracts XML, pretty-prints, merges adjacent runs, and converts smart quotes to XML entities (`“` etc.) so they survive editing. Use `--merge-runs false` to skip run merging.
   407	
   408	### Step 2: Edit XML
   409	
   410	Edit files in `unpacked/word/`. See XML Reference below for patterns.
   411	
   412	**Use "Claude" as the author** for tracked changes and comments, unless the user explicitly requests use of a different name.
   413	
   414	**Use the Edit tool directly for string replacement. Do not write Python scripts.** Scripts introduce unnecessary complexity. The Edit tool shows exactly what is being replaced.
   415	
   416	**CRITICAL: Use smart quotes for new content.** When adding text with apostrophes or quotes, use XML entities to produce smart quotes:
   417	```xml
   418	<!-- Use these entities for professional typography -->
   419	<w:t>Here’s a quote: “Hello”</w:t>
   420	```
   421	| Entity | Character |
   422	|--------|-----------|
   423	| `‘` | ‘ (left single) |
   424	| `’` | ’ (right single / apostrophe) |
   425	| `“` | “ (left double) |
   426	| `”` | ” (right double) |
   427	
   428	**Adding comments:** Use `comment.py` to handle boilerplate across multiple XML files (text must be pre-escaped XML):
   429	```bash
   430	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Comment text with & and ’"
   431	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 1 "Reply text" --parent 0  # reply to comment 0
   432	python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 "Text" --author "Custom Author"  # custom author name
   433	```
   434	Then add markers to document.xml (see Comments in XML Reference).
   435	
   436	### Step 3: Pack
   437	```bash
   438	python scripts/office/pack.py unpacked/ output.docx --original document.docx
   439	```
   440	Validates with auto-repair, condenses XML, and creates DOCX. Use `--validate false` to skip.
   441	
   442	**Auto-repair will fix:**
   443	- `durableId` >= 0x7FFFFFFF (regenerates valid ID)
   444	- Missing `xml:space="preserve"` on `<w:t>` with whitespace
   445	
   446	**Auto-repair won't fix:**
   447	- Malformed XML, invalid element nesting, missing relationships, schema violations
   448	
   449	### Common Pitfalls
   450	
   451	- **Replace entire `<w:r>` elements**: When adding tracked changes, replace the whole `<w:r>...</w:r>` block with `<w:del>...<w:ins>...` as siblings. Don't inject tracked change tags inside a run.
   452	- **Preserve `<w:rPr>` formatting**: Copy the original run's `<w:rPr>` block into your tracked change runs to maintain bold, font size, etc.
   453	
   454	---
   455	
   456	## XML Reference
   457	
   458	### Schema Compliance
   459	
   460	- **Element order in `<w:pPr>`**: `<w:pStyle>`, `<w:numPr>`, `<w:spacing>`, `<w:ind>`, `<w:jc>`, `<w:rPr>` last
   461	- **Whitespace**: Add `xml:space="preserve"` to `<w:t>` with leading/trailing spaces
   462	- **RSIDs**: Must be 8-digit hex (e.g., `00AB1234`)
   463	
   464	### Tracked Changes
   465	
   466	**Insertion:**
   467	```xml
   468	<w:ins w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   469	  <w:r><w:t>inserted text</w:t></w:r>
   470	</w:ins>
   471	```
   472	
   473	**Deletion:**
   474	```xml
   475	<w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   476	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   477	</w:del>
   478	```
   479	
   480	**Inside `<w:del>`**: Use `<w:delText>` instead of `<w:t>`, and `<w:delInstrText>` instead of `<w:instrText>`.
   481	
   482	**Minimal edits** - only mark what changes:
   483	```xml
   484	<!-- Change "30 days" to "60 days" -->
   485	<w:r><w:t>The term is </w:t></w:r>
   486	<w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   487	  <w:r><w:delText>30</w:delText></w:r>
   488	</w:del>
   489	<w:ins w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="...">
   490	  <w:r><w:t>60</w:t></w:r>
   491	</w:ins>
   492	<w:r><w:t> days.</w:t></w:r>
   493	```
   494	
   495	**Deleting entire paragraphs/list items** - when removing ALL content from a paragraph, also mark the paragraph mark as deleted so it merges with the next paragraph. Add `<w:del/>` inside `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`:
   496	```xml
   497	<w:p>
   498	  <w:pPr>
   499	    <w:numPr>...</w:numPr>  <!-- list numbering if present -->
   500	    <w:rPr>
   501	      <w:del w:id="1" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"/>
   502	    </w:rPr>
   503	  </w:pPr>
   504	  <w:del w:id="2" w:author="Claude" w:date="2025-01-01T00:00:00Z">
   505	    <w:r><w:delText>Entire paragraph content being deleted...</w:delText></w:r>
   506	  </w:del>
   507	</w:p>
   508	```
   509	Without the `<w:del/>` in `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`, accepting changes leaves an empty paragraph/list item.
   510	
   511	**Rejecting another author's insertion** - nest deletion inside their insertion:
   512	```xml
   513	<w:ins w:author="Jane" w:id="5">
   514	  <w:del w:author="Claude" w:id="10">
   515	    <w:r><w:delText>their inserted text</w:delText></w:r>
   516	  </w:del>
   517	</w:ins>
   518	```
   519	
   520	**Restoring another author's deletion** - add insertion after (don't modify their deletion):
   521	```xml
   522	<w:del w:author="Jane" w:id="5">
   523	  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>
   524	</w:del>
   525	<w:ins w:author="Claude" w:id="10">
   526	  <w:r><w:t>deleted text</w:t></w:r>
   527	</w:ins>
   528	```
   529	
   530	### Comments
   531

/**
 * @file ProcessMemoryPool.hpp
 * @brief Process-wide fixed-size block pool with lock-free allocation.
 *
 * ProcessMemoryPool is the mechanical core of Chevron's memory hierarchy.
 * It acquires large chunks of memory from the operating system, carves them
 * into fixed-size blocks, and distributes those blocks to downstream
 * components through a lock-free embedded free list.
 *
 * This class is not used directly by downstream consumers. It is composed
 * as a value member inside MemoryCore, which provides the policy surface
 * (budget enforcement, preallocation, acquire/release interface) on top of
 * the pool's mechanical operations.
 *
 * @note Thread-safe. All allocation and deallocation operations are lock-free.
 *
 * Chevron Library — Internal Infrastructure
 */

#ifndef CHEVRON_MEMORY_PROCESS_MEMORY_POOL_HPP
#define CHEVRON_MEMORY_PROCESS_MEMORY_POOL_HPP

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

namespace chevron::memory {

// ============================================================================
// Supporting Types
// ============================================================================

/**
 * @brief Lightweight value type describing a contiguous region of memory.
 *
 * Carries a base pointer and byte size. Does not own the memory it describes.
 * Used as the currency for memory transfer between hierarchy components.
 */
struct MemoryRegion
{
    void* base;         ///< Starting address of the region.
    std::size_t size;   ///< Size of the region in bytes.
};


/**
 * @brief Descriptor for a single acquired chunk of OS memory.
 *
 * Stored in the pool's chunk descriptor array. Records the base address
 * and size of each chunk so that all chunks can be released back to the
 * OS at pool destruction.
 */
struct ChunkDescriptor
{
    void* base;         ///< Starting address returned by the OS allocation call.
    std::size_t size;   ///< Size of the chunk in bytes.
};


/**
 * @brief Tagged pointer for ABA-safe lock-free operations on the free list.
 *
 * Pairs a block pointer with a monotonically increasing generation counter.
 * The counter increments on every push or pop, ensuring that a CAS operation
 * detects any intervening modifications even if the pointer value returns to
 * a previously observed state.
 *
 * @note This type must be 16 bytes and lock-free under std::atomic to
 *       guarantee the pool's lock-free contract. A static assertion in
 *       ProcessMemoryPool enforces this at compile time.
 */
struct TaggedPointer
{
    void* ptr;                  ///< Pointer to a free block (or nullptr if list is empty).
    std::uint64_t generation;   ///< Monotonically increasing operation counter.
};


/**
 * @brief Construction parameters for ProcessMemoryPool.
 *
 * Bundles all construction-time configuration into a single value type,
 * keeping the constructor signature clean and self-documenting.
 */
struct PoolConfig
{
    std::size_t block_size;             ///< Size of each block in bytes (before alignment adjustment).
    std::size_t block_alignment;        ///< Alignment guarantee for every block's starting address.
    std::size_t chunk_size;             ///< Size of each OS-acquired chunk in bytes.
    std::size_t budget_ceiling;         ///< Maximum total bytes the pool may acquire from the OS.
    std::size_t initial_thread_batch;   ///< Starting batch size for thread-local geometric growth.
    std::size_t max_thread_batch;       ///< Maximum batch size a thread may claim in one trip.
};


// ============================================================================
// ProcessMemoryPool
// ============================================================================

/**
 * @class ProcessMemoryPool
 * @brief Lock-free fixed-size block pool with embedded free list and
 *        per-thread geometric caching.
 *
 * ## Mechanical Overview
 *
 * The pool acquires large contiguous chunks from the OS via aligned
 * allocation and carves each chunk into fixed-size blocks. Free blocks
 * are linked together through an embedded singly-linked list — each free
 * block stores a pointer to the next free block in its own memory. The
 * list head is an atomic tagged pointer (pointer + generation counter)
 * that supports ABA-safe compare-and-swap for lock-free push and pop.
 *
 * ## Thread-Local Caching
 *
 * To reduce contention on the shared free list, each thread maintains a
 * private cache of blocks. When the cache is empty, the thread acquires
 * a batch from the shared list. The batch size starts at a configured
 * initial value and doubles on each subsequent trip (geometric growth),
 * up to a configured maximum. This keeps high-demand threads away from
 * the shared atomics on the common allocation path.
 *
 * ## Growth Model
 *
 * The pool starts empty and acquires chunks lazily as demand requires,
 * up to the configured budget ceiling. Once the ceiling is reached,
 * further growth requests result in std::bad_alloc. Chunks are never
 * returned to the OS during runtime — all OS-level deallocation occurs
 * at pool destruction.
 *
 * ## Ownership
 *
 * ProcessMemoryPool is composed inside MemoryCore as a value member.
 * It is not intended for direct use by downstream consumers.
 */
class ProcessMemoryPool
{
public:
    // === Lifecycle ===========================================================

    /**
     * @brief Constructs the pool with the given configuration.
     *
     * Validates and adjusts configuration parameters:
     * - block_size is rounded up to the nearest multiple of block_alignment.
     * - block_size is enforced to be at least sizeof(void*).
     * - chunk_size is rounded up to the nearest multiple of effective block_size.
     * - max_chunk_count is derived from budget_ceiling / chunk_size.
     * - The chunk descriptor array is allocated to hold max_chunk_count entries.
     *
     * No OS memory is acquired for blocks at this point. The pool starts
     * with an empty free list and zero chunks. Use preallocate() to
     * acquire initial chunks before the pool enters active use.
     *
     * @param config Construction-time configuration parameters.
     *
     * @throws std::invalid_argument if block_size is zero, chunk_size is zero,
     *         budget_ceiling is zero, or budget_ceiling < chunk_size.
     */
    explicit ProcessMemoryPool(const PoolConfig& config);

    /**
     * @brief Destroys the pool and releases all chunks back to the OS.
     *
     * All chunks tracked in the descriptor array are released. Thread-local
     * caches are not drained — their blocks reside within chunks that are
     * being released as whole units, so individual block cleanup is unnecessary.
     */
    ~ProcessMemoryPool();

    ProcessMemoryPool(const ProcessMemoryPool&) = delete;
    ProcessMemoryPool& operator=(const ProcessMemoryPool&) = delete;
    ProcessMemoryPool(ProcessMemoryPool&&) = delete;
    ProcessMemoryPool& operator=(ProcessMemoryPool&&) = delete;


    // === Core Operations =====================================================

    /**
     * @brief Acquires a single block from the pool.
     *
     * Attempts to pop a block from the calling thread's local cache first.
     * If the local cache is empty, acquires a batch from the shared free
     * list (triggering chunk growth if the shared list is also exhausted)
     * and refills the local cache before returning a block.
     *
     * @return Pointer to the acquired block, aligned to block_alignment.
     *
     * @throws std::bad_alloc if the pool is exhausted (budget ceiling reached
     *         and all blocks are allocated).
     */
    [[nodiscard]] void* allocate();

    /**
     * @brief Returns a single block to the pool.
     *
     * Pushes the block onto the calling thread's local cache. If the local
     * cache exceeds a drain threshold, a batch is returned to the shared
     * free list to make blocks available to other threads.
     *
     * @param block Pointer to the block being returned. Must have been
     *              obtained from this pool's allocate(). Passing a pointer
     *              not obtained from this pool is undefined behavior.
     */
    void deallocate(void* block) noexcept;

    /**
     * @brief Acquires one or more chunks from the OS to prepopulate the pool.
     *
     * Each acquired chunk is carved into blocks and threaded into the shared
     * free list. Intended to be called during initialization before the pool
     * enters active concurrent use, avoiding growth-path synchronization
     * during runtime.
     *
     * @param chunk_count Number of chunks to acquire.
     *
     * @throws std::bad_alloc if acquiring the requested chunks would exceed
     *         the budget ceiling.
     */
    void preallocate(std::size_t chunk_count);


    // === Diagnostics =========================================================

    /**
     * @brief Returns the effective block size after alignment adjustment.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t effective_block_size() const noexcept;

    /**
     * @brief Returns the block alignment guarantee.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t alignment() const noexcept;

    /**
     * @brief Returns the number of chunks currently acquired from the OS.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t acquired_chunk_count() const noexcept;

    /**
     * @brief Returns the maximum number of chunks the pool may acquire.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t max_chunks() const noexcept;

    /**
     * @brief Returns the total number of blocks across all acquired chunks.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t total_block_count() const noexcept;

    /**
     * @brief Returns the current generation counter from the free list head.
     *
     * This counter increments on every push and pop operation against the
     * shared free list. It serves primarily as the ABA guard but also
     * provides a total operation count for diagnostics.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t generation() const noexcept;


private:
    // === Internal Operations =================================================

    /**
     * @brief Acquires a new chunk from the OS and integrates it into the pool.
     *
     * Allocates aligned memory, records the chunk in the descriptor array,
     * carves the chunk into blocks, and threads those blocks into the shared
     * free list.
     *
     * @throws std::bad_alloc if the budget ceiling would be exceeded or if
     *         the OS allocation fails.
     */
    void grow();

    /**
     * @brief Carves a raw chunk into blocks and threads them into the free list.
     *
     * Walks the chunk from base to end, writing embedded next-pointers into
     * each block to form a singly-linked chain of free blocks. The chain is
     * then prepended to the shared free list via CAS.
     *
     * @param chunk_base Starting address of the chunk (must be aligned).
     * @param chunk_size Size of the chunk in bytes.
     */
    void carve_and_thread(void* chunk_base, std::size_t chunk_size);

    /**
     * @brief Pops a batch of blocks from the shared free list into a
     *        thread-local cache.
     *
     * Walks the free list to find the Nth block, then CAS-swaps the head
     * to the block after the Nth, detaching the entire batch in a single
     * atomic operation. Retries on CAS failure.
     *
     * @param batch_size Number of blocks to pop.
     * @return Pointer to the head of the detached chain, or nullptr if
     *         insufficient blocks are available.
     */
    void* pop_batch(std::size_t batch_size);

    /**
     * @brief Pushes a chain of blocks from a thread-local cache back onto
     *        the shared free list.
     *
     * Links the chain's tail to the current head and CAS-swaps the head
     * to the chain's first block, prepending the entire batch in a single
     * atomic operation. Retries on CAS failure.
     *
     * @param head Pointer to the first block in the chain.
     * @param tail Pointer to the last block in the chain.
     */
    void push_batch(void* head, void* tail);

    /**
     * @brief Platform-specific aligned memory acquisition from the OS.
     *
     * Acquires a contiguous region of at least the requested size with
     * the specified alignment. The returned pointer must be freed with
     * release_to_os().
     *
     * @param size Number of bytes to acquire.
     * @param alignment Required alignment of the returned address.
     * @return Pointer to the acquired region.
     *
     * @throws std::bad_alloc if the OS refuses the allocation.
     */
    static void* acquire_from_os(std::size_t size, std::size_t alignment);

    /**
     * @brief Platform-specific memory release back to the OS.
     *
     * Releases a region previously acquired by acquire_from_os().
     *
     * @param base Starting address of the region.
     * @param size Size of the region in bytes.
     */
    static void release_to_os(void* base, std::size_t size) noexcept;


    // === Thread-Local Cache ==================================================

    /**
     * @brief Per-thread cache state for geometric batch growth.
     *
     * Each thread that interacts with the pool maintains one of these
     * structures in thread-local storage. The local free list uses the
     * same embedded next-pointer scheme as the shared free list but
     * requires no atomic operations since only the owning thread touches it.
     */
    struct ThreadCache
    {
        void* free_list_head;           ///< Head of the thread-local free block chain.
        std::size_t cached_count;       ///< Number of blocks currently in the local cache.
        std::size_t current_batch_size; ///< Batch size for the next trip to the shared pool.
    };

    /**
     * @brief Retrieves or initializes the calling thread's cache.
     */
    ThreadCache& thread_cache();


    // === Member State ========================================================

    // -- Free list (shared, contended) --
    std::atomic<TaggedPointer> free_list_head_;  ///< ABA-safe head of the embedded free list.

    // -- Pool geometry (constant after construction) --
    std::size_t block_size_;            ///< Effective block size (aligned, >= sizeof(void*)).
    std::size_t block_alignment_;       ///< Alignment guarantee for block starting addresses.
    std::size_t chunk_size_;            ///< Size of each OS-acquired chunk in bytes.
    std::size_t blocks_per_chunk_;      ///< Number of blocks carved from each chunk.
    std::size_t budget_ceiling_;        ///< Maximum total bytes acquirable from the OS.

    // -- Chunk tracking (grows monotonically, never shrinks) --
    ChunkDescriptor* chunk_descriptors_;  ///< Fixed array of chunk descriptors.
    std::size_t chunk_count_;             ///< Number of chunks currently acquired.
    std::size_t max_chunk_count_;         ///< Capacity of the chunk descriptor array.

    // -- Thread-local cache parameters (constant after construction) --
    std::size_t initial_thread_batch_;  ///< Starting batch size for geometric growth.
    std::size_t max_thread_batch_;      ///< Maximum batch size cap per thread.

    // -- Compile-time guarantees --
    static_assert(
        std::atomic<TaggedPointer>::is_always_lock_free,
        "ProcessMemoryPool requires lock-free 16-byte atomics. "
        "The target platform does not support lock-free std::atomic<TaggedPointer>."
    );
};

} // namespace chevron::memory

#endif // CHEVRON_MEMORY_PROCESS_MEMORY_POOL_HPP

     * This counter increments on every push and pop operation against the
     * shared free list. It serves primarily as the ABA guard but also
     * provides a total operation count for diagnostics.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t generation() const noexcept;


private:
    // === Internal Operations =================================================

    /**
     * @brief Acquires a new chunk from the OS and integrates it into the pool.
     *
     * Allocates aligned memory, records the chunk in the descriptor array,
     * carves the chunk into blocks, and threads those blocks into the shared
     * free list.
     *
     * @throws std::bad_alloc if the budget ceiling would be exceeded or if
     *         the OS allocation fails.
     */
    void grow();

    /**
     * @brief Carves a raw chunk into blocks and threads them into the free list.
     *
     * Walks the chunk from base to end, writing embedded next-pointers into
     * each block to form a singly-linked chain of free blocks. The chain is
     * then prepended to the shared free list via CAS.
     *
     * @param chunk_base Starting address of the chunk (must be aligned).
     * @param chunk_size Size of the chunk in bytes.
     */
    void carve_and_thread(void* chunk_base, std::size_t chunk_size);

    /**
     * @brief Pops a batch of blocks from the shared free list into a
     *        thread-local cache.
     *
     * Walks the free list to find the Nth block, then CAS-swaps the head
     * to the block after the Nth, detaching the entire batch in a single
     * atomic operation. Retries on CAS failure.
     *
     * @param batch_size Number of blocks to pop.
     * @return Pointer to the head of the detached chain, or nullptr if
     *         insufficient blocks are available.
     */
    void* pop_batch(std::size_t batch_size);

    /**
     * @brief Pushes a chain of blocks from a thread-local cache back onto
     *        the shared free list.
     *
     * Links the chain's tail to the current head and CAS-swaps the head
     * to the chain's first block, prepending the entire batch in a single
     * atomic operation. Retries on CAS failure.
     *
     * @param head Pointer to the first block in the chain.
     * @param tail Pointer to the last block in the chain.
     */
    void push_batch(void* head, void* tail);

    /**
     * @brief Platform-specific aligned memory acquisition from the OS.
     *
     * Acquires a contiguous region of at least the requested size with
     * the specified alignment. The returned pointer must be freed with
     * release_to_os().
     *
     * @param size Number of bytes to acquire.
     * @param alignment Required alignment of the returned address.
     * @return Pointer to the acquired region.
     *
     * @throws std::bad_alloc if the OS refuses the allocation.
     */
    static void* acquire_from_os(std::size_t size, std::size_t alignment);

    /**
     * @brief Platform-specific memory release back to the OS.
     *
     * Releases a region previously acquired by acquire_from_os().
     *
     * @param base Starting address of the region.
     * @param size Size of the region in bytes.
     */
    static void release_to_os(void* base, std::size_t size) noexcept;


    // === Thread-Local Cache ==================================================

    /**
     * @brief Per-thread cache state for geometric batch growth.
     *
     * Each thread that interacts with the pool maintains one of these
     * structures in thread-local storage. The local free list uses the
     * same embedded next-pointer scheme as the shared free list but
     * requires no atomic operations since only the owning thread touches it.
     */
    struct ThreadCache
    {
        void* free_list_head;           ///< Head of the thread-local free block chain.
        std::size_t cached_count;       ///< Number of blocks currently in the local cache.
        std::size_t current_batch_size; ///< Batch size for the next trip to the shared pool.
    };

    /**
     * @brief Retrieves or initializes the calling thread's cache.
     */
    ThreadCache& thread_cache();


    // === Member State ========================================================

    // -- Free list (shared, contended) --
    std::atomic<TaggedPointer> free_list_head_;  ///< ABA-safe head of the embedded free list.

    // -- Pool geometry (constant after construction) --
    std::size_t block_size_;            ///< Effective block size (aligned, >= sizeof(void*)).
    std::size_t block_alignment_;       ///< Alignment guarantee for block starting addresses.
    std::size_t chunk_size_;            ///< Size of each OS-acquired chunk in bytes.
    std::size_t blocks_per_chunk_;      ///< Number of blocks carved from each chunk.
    std::size_t budget_ceiling_;        ///< Maximum total bytes acquirable from the OS.

    // -- Chunk tracking (grows monotonically, never shrinks) --
    ChunkDescriptor* chunk_descriptors_;  ///< Fixed array of chunk descriptors.
    std::size_t chunk_count_;             ///< Number of chunks currently acquired.
    std::size_t max_chunk_count_;         ///< Capacity of the chunk descriptor array.

    // -- Thread-local cache parameters (constant after construction) --
    std::size_t initial_thread_batch_;  ///< Starting batch size for geometric growth.
    std::size_t max_thread_batch_;      ///< Maximum batch size cap per thread.

    // -- Compile-time guarantees --
    static_assert(
        std::atomic<TaggedPointer>::is_always_lock_free,
        "ProcessMemoryPool requires lock-free 16-byte atomics. "
        "The target platform does not support lock-free std::atomic<TaggedPointer>."
    );
};

Great questions, let me address each one.

**On `ThreadCache` and `thread_cache()`**

You're not missing something — I intentionally left the storage mechanism unexpressed in the header because there are a few ways to do it, and I wanted to discuss it before committing. The approach I had in mind is a `thread_local` static variable inside the `thread_cache()` method body. When a thread calls `thread_cache()` for the first time, the `thread_local` static is initialized with an empty cache, and every subsequent call from that thread returns the same instance. No member variable on the pool is needed because the storage lives in the thread itself, not in the pool object.

However, there's a problem with this approach that I should have flagged. A `thread_local` static inside the method gives you one `ThreadCache` per thread, period. If there were ever two `ProcessMemoryPool` instances in the same process (which your design doesn't intend, but a library should be defensive about), both pools would share the same `ThreadCache` on each thread. The thread would be caching blocks from pool A and accidentally returning them to pool B.

The safer approach is a `thread_local` storage mechanism keyed by pool instance — something like a `thread_local` map or a `thread_local` pointer that the pool registers itself into. But that adds overhead and complexity.

Given that your design has exactly one `ProcessMemoryPool` per process (composed inside the single `MemoryCore`), the simple `thread_local` static inside the method body works correctly and has zero lookup overhead. If you want to be defensive, we can add a debug-mode assertion that checks the block actually belongs to this pool instance. My recommendation is the simple approach with the debug assertion.

**On `FreeRegionNode`**

Yes, absolutely. A dedicated struct makes the embedded free list explicit in the code rather than hiding it behind raw `void*` casts scattered through the implementation. `FreeRegionNode` with a single `void* next` member is exactly right. When a block is free, its first `sizeof(FreeRegionNode)` bytes are interpreted as a `FreeRegionNode`. When it's allocated, those bytes belong to the caller and the node ceases to exist. Having the struct makes that reinterpretation explicit and clean — you `reinterpret_cast<FreeRegionNode*>(block)` in exactly the places where you're treating a free block as a list node, and the cast documents the intent.

**On `effective_block_size()` vs. `block_size()`**

You're right to push on this — the name is confusing. Here's what I was trying to express. The caller passes in a `block_size` in the `PoolConfig`, say 48 bytes. The pool rounds that up to a multiple of the alignment, say 64 bytes. The "effective" block size is 64 — the actual size of each block in memory. But calling it "effective" implies there's another version that returns the original 48, which there isn't and shouldn't be. Once the pool has adjusted the size, the original value is irrelevant. The pool operates entirely in terms of the adjusted size.

So you're right — it should just be `block_size()`. The adjustment happens at construction, the result is stored in `block_size_`, and that's the only block size that exists. The word "effective" was me over-clarifying something that doesn't need clarification. Drop it.

**On the `FreeListHead` alias**

Good call. `std::atomic<TaggedPointer>` as a raw type on the member says nothing about its role. `FreeListHead` makes the member declaration self-documenting — when you read `FreeListHead free_list_head_` you immediately know what it is without checking the type definition. The alias belongs as a private nested type since it's an implementation detail of how the free list is represented.

---

So to summarize the changes before I touch anything: simple `thread_local` static approach for `ThreadCache` with a debug assertion for pool identity, add `FreeRegionNode` as a nested struct with a single `void* next` member, rename `effective_block_size()` to `block_size()`, and add a private `using FreeListHead = std::atomic<TaggedPointer>` alias. Does that all track, or do you want to adjust anything before I update the header?

1	/**
     2	 * @file ProcessMemoryPool.hpp
     3	 * @brief Process-wide fixed-size block pool with lock-free allocation.
     4	 *
     5	 * ProcessMemoryPool is the mechanical core of Chevron's memory hierarchy.
     6	 * It acquires large chunks of memory from the operating system, carves them
     7	 * into fixed-size blocks, and distributes those blocks to downstream
     8	 * components through a lock-free embedded free list.
     9	 *
    10	 * This class is not used directly by downstream consumers. It is composed
    11	 * as a value member inside MemoryCore, which provides the policy surface
    12	 * (budget enforcement, preallocation, acquire/release interface) on top of
    13	 * the pool's mechanical operations.
    14	 *
    15	 * @note Thread-safe. All allocation and deallocation operations are lock-free.
    16	 *
    17	 * Chevron Library — Internal Infrastructure
    18	 */
    19	
    20	#ifndef CHEVRON_MEMORY_PROCESS_MEMORY_POOL_HPP
    21	#define CHEVRON_MEMORY_PROCESS_MEMORY_POOL_HPP
    22	
    23	#include <atomic>
    24	#include <cstddef>
    25	#include <cstdint>
    26	
    27	namespace chevron::memory {
    28	
    29	// ============================================================================
    30	// Supporting Types
    31	// ============================================================================
    32	
    33	/**
    34	 * @brief Lightweight value type describing a contiguous region of memory.
    35	 *
    36	 * Carries a base pointer and byte size. Does not own the memory it describes.
    37	 * Used as the currency for memory transfer between hierarchy components.
    38	 */
    39	struct MemoryRegion
    40	{
    41	    void* base;         ///< Starting address of the region.
    42	    std::size_t size;   ///< Size of the region in bytes.
    43	};
    44	
    45	
    46	/**
    47	 * @brief Descriptor for a single acquired chunk of OS memory.
    48	 *
    49	 * Stored in the pool's chunk descriptor array. Records the base address
    50	 * and size of each chunk so that all chunks can be released back to the
    51	 * OS at pool destruction.
    52	 */
    53	struct ChunkDescriptor
    54	{
    55	    void* base;         ///< Starting address returned by the OS allocation call.
    56	    std::size_t size;   ///< Size of the chunk in bytes.
    57	};
    58	
    59	
    60	/**
    61	 * @brief Tagged pointer for ABA-safe lock-free operations on the free list.
    62	 *
    63	 * Pairs a block pointer with a monotonically increasing generation counter.
    64	 * The counter increments on every push or pop, ensuring that a CAS operation
    65	 * detects any intervening modifications even if the pointer value returns to
    66	 * a previously observed state.
    67	 *
    68	 * @note This type must be 16 bytes and lock-free under std::atomic to
    69	 *       guarantee the pool's lock-free contract. A static assertion in
    70	 *       ProcessMemoryPool enforces this at compile time.
    71	 */
    72	struct TaggedPointer
    73	{
    74	    void* ptr;                  ///< Pointer to a free block (or nullptr if list is empty).
    75	    std::uint64_t generation;   ///< Monotonically increasing operation counter.
    76	};
    77	
    78	
    79	/**
    80	 * @brief Construction parameters for ProcessMemoryPool.
    81	 *
    82	 * Bundles all construction-time configuration into a single value type,
    83	 * keeping the constructor signature clean and self-documenting.
    84	 */
    85	struct PoolConfig
    86	{
    87	    std::size_t block_size;             ///< Size of each block in bytes (before alignment adjustment).
    88	    std::size_t block_alignment;        ///< Alignment guarantee for every block's starting address.
    89	    std::size_t chunk_size;             ///< Size of each OS-acquired chunk in bytes.
    90	    std::size_t budget_ceiling;         ///< Maximum total bytes the pool may acquire from the OS.
    91	    std::size_t initial_thread_batch;   ///< Starting batch size for thread-local geometric growth.
    92	    std::size_t max_thread_batch;       ///< Maximum batch size a thread may claim in one trip.
    93	};
    94	
    95	
    96	// ============================================================================
    97	// ProcessMemoryPool
    98	// ============================================================================
    99	
   100	/**
   101	 * @class ProcessMemoryPool
   102	 * @brief Lock-free fixed-size block pool with embedded free list and
   103	 *        per-thread geometric caching.
   104	 *
   105	 * ## Mechanical Overview
   106	 *
   107	 * The pool acquires large contiguous chunks from the OS via aligned
   108	 * allocation and carves each chunk into fixed-size blocks. Free blocks
   109	 * are linked together through an embedded singly-linked list — each free
   110	 * block stores a pointer to the next free block in its own memory. The
   111	 * list head is an atomic tagged pointer (pointer + generation counter)
   112	 * that supports ABA-safe compare-and-swap for lock-free push and pop.
   113	 *
   114	 * ## Thread-Local Caching
   115	 *
   116	 * To reduce contention on the shared free list, each thread maintains a
   117	 * private cache of blocks. When the cache is empty, the thread acquires
   118	 * a batch from the shared list. The batch size starts at a configured
   119	 * initial value and doubles on each subsequent trip (geometric growth),
   120	 * up to a configured maximum. This keeps high-demand threads away from
   121	 * the shared atomics on the common allocation path.
   122	 *
   123	 * ## Growth Model
   124	 *
   125	 * The pool starts empty and acquires chunks lazily as demand requires,
   126	 * up to the configured budget ceiling. Once the ceiling is reached,
   127	 * further growth requests result in std::bad_alloc. Chunks are never
   128	 * returned to the OS during runtime — all OS-level deallocation occurs
   129	 * at pool destruction.
   130	 *
   131	 * ## Ownership
   132	 *
   133	 * ProcessMemoryPool is composed inside MemoryCore as a value member.
   134	 * It is not intended for direct use by downstream consumers.
   135	 */
   136	class ProcessMemoryPool
   137	{
   138	public:
   139	    // === Lifecycle ===========================================================
   140	
   141	    /**
   142	     * @brief Constructs the pool with the given configuration.
   143	     *
   144	     * Validates and adjusts configuration parameters:
   145	     * - block_size is rounded up to the nearest multiple of block_alignment.
   146	     * - block_size is enforced to be at least sizeof(void*).
   147	     * - chunk_size is rounded up to the nearest multiple of effective block_size.
   148	     * - max_chunk_count is derived from budget_ceiling / chunk_size.
   149	     * - The chunk descriptor array is allocated to hold max_chunk_count entries.
   150	     *
   151	     * No OS memory is acquired for blocks at this point. The pool starts
   152	     * with an empty free list and zero chunks. Use preallocate() to
   153	     * acquire initial chunks before the pool enters active use.
   154	     *
   155	     * @param config Construction-time configuration parameters.
   156	     *
   157	     * @throws std::invalid_argument if block_size is zero, chunk_size is zero,
   158	     *         budget_ceiling is zero, or budget_ceiling < chunk_size.
   159	     */
   160	    explicit ProcessMemoryPool(const PoolConfig& config);
   161	
   162	    /**
   163	     * @brief Destroys the pool and releases all chunks back to the OS.
   164	     *
   165	     * All chunks tracked in the descriptor array are released. Thread-local
   166	     * caches are not drained — their blocks reside within chunks that are
   167	     * being released as whole units, so individual block cleanup is unnecessary.
   168	     */

   171	    ProcessMemoryPool(const ProcessMemoryPool&) = delete;
   172	    ProcessMemoryPool& operator=(const ProcessMemoryPool&) = delete;
   173	    ProcessMemoryPool(ProcessMemoryPool&&) = delete;
   174	    ProcessMemoryPool& operator=(ProcessMemoryPool&&) = delete;

   176	
   177	    // === Core Operations =====================================================

   179	    /**
   180	     * @brief Acquires a single block from the pool.
   181	     *
   182	     * Attempts to pop a block from the calling thread's local cache first.
   183	     * If the local cache is empty, acquires a batch from the shared free
   184	     * list (triggering chunk growth if the shared list is also exhausted)
   185	     * and refills the local cache before returning a block.
   186	     *

   188	     *
   189	     * @throws std::bad_alloc if the pool is exhausted (budget ceiling reached

   191	     */
   192	    [[nodiscard]] void* allocate();
   193	
   194	    /**
   195	     * @brief Returns a single block to the pool.
   196	     *
   197	     * Pushes the block onto the calling thread's local cache. If the local
   198	     * cache exceeds a drain threshold, a batch is returned to the shared
   199	     * free list to make blocks available to other threads.
   200	     *
   201	     * @param block Pointer to the block being returned. Must have been
   202	     *              obtained from this pool's allocate(). Passing a pointer
   203	     *              not obtained from this pool is undefined behavior.
   204	     */
   205	    void deallocate(void* block) noexcept;
   206	
   207	    /**
   208	     * @brief Acquires one or more chunks from the OS to prepopulate the pool.
   209	     *
   210	     * Each acquired chunk is carved into blocks and threaded into the shared
   211	     * free list. Intended to be called during initialization before the pool
   212	     * enters active concurrent use, avoiding growth-path synchronization
   213	     * during runtime.
   214	     *

   216	     *
   217	     * @throws std::bad_alloc if acquiring the requested chunks would exceed
   218	     *         the budget ceiling.
   219	     */
   220	    void preallocate(std::size_t chunk_count);
   221	
   222	
   223	    // === Diagnostics =========================================================
   224	
   225	    /**
   226	     * @brief Returns the effective block size after alignment adjustment.
   227	     */
   228	    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t effective_block_size() const noexcept;
   229	
   230	    /**
   231	     * @brief Returns the block alignment guarantee.
   232	     */

   234	
   235	    /**
   236	     * @brief Returns the number of chunks currently acquired from the OS.
   237	     */

   239	
   240	    /**
   241	     * @brief Returns the maximum number of chunks the pool may acquire.
   242	     */
   243	    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t max_chunks() const noexcept;
   244	
   245	    /**
   246	     * @brief Returns the total number of blocks across all acquired chunks.
   247	     */
   248	    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t total_block_count() const noexcept;
   249	
   250	    /**
   251	     * @brief Returns the current generation counter from the free list head.
   252	     *
   253	     * This counter increments on every push and pop operation against the
   254	     * shared free list. It serves primarily as the ABA guard but also
   255	     * provides a total operation count for diagnostics.
   256	     */
   257	    [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t generation() const noexcept;
   258	
   259	
   260	private:
   261	    // === Internal Operations =================================================
   262	
   263	    /**
   264	     * @brief Acquires a new chunk from the OS and integrates it into the pool.
   265	     *
   266	     * Allocates aligned memory, records the chunk in the descriptor array,
   267	     * carves the chunk into blocks, and threads those blocks into the shared
   268	     * free list.
   269	     *
   270	     * @throws std::bad_alloc if the budget ceiling would be exceeded or if
   271	     *         the OS allocation fails.
   272	     */
   273	    void grow();
   274	
   275	    /**

   277	     *
   278	     * Walks the chunk from base to end, writing embedded next-pointers into
   279	     * each block to form a singly-linked chain of free blocks. The chain is
   280	     * then prepended to the shared free list via CAS.
   281	     *
   282	     * @param chunk_base Starting address of the chunk (must be aligned).
   283	     * @param chunk_size Size of the chunk in bytes.
   284	     */
   285	    void carve_and_thread(void* chunk_base, std::size_t chunk_size);
   286	
   287	    /**

   289	     *        thread-local cache.
   290	     *

   292	     * to the block after the Nth, detaching the entire batch in a single
   293	     * atomic operation. Retries on CAS failure.
   294	     *
   295	     * @param batch_size Number of blocks to pop.
   296	     * @return Pointer to the head of the detached chain, or nullptr if
   297	     *         insufficient blocks are available.
   298	     */
   299	    void* pop_batch(std::size_t batch_size);
   300	
   301	    /**

   303	     *        the shared free list.
   304	     *
   305	     * Links the chain's tail to the current head and CAS-swaps the head
   306	     * to the chain's first block, prepending the entire batch in a single
   307	     * atomic operation. Retries on CAS failure.
   308	     *

   310	     * @param tail Pointer to the last block in the chain.
   311	     */
   312	    void push_batch(void* head, void* tail);
   313	
   314	    /**

   317	     * Acquires a contiguous region of at least the requested size with
   318	     * the specified alignment. The returned pointer must be freed with
   319	     * release_to_os().
   320	     *
   321	     * @param size Number of bytes to acquire.
   322	     * @param alignment Required alignment of the returned address.
   323	     * @return Pointer to the acquired region.
   324	     *
   325	     * @throws std::bad_alloc if the OS refuses the allocation.
   326	     */
   327	    static void* acquire_from_os(std::size_t size, std::size_t alignment);
   328	
   329	    /**
   330	     * @brief Platform-specific memory release back to the OS.
   331	     *
   332	     * Releases a region previously acquired by acquire_from_os().
   333	     *
   334	     * @param base Starting address of the region.
   335	     * @param size Size of the region in bytes.
   336	     */
   337	    static void release_to_os(void* base, std::size_t size) noexcept;
   338	
   339	
   340	    // === Thread-Local Cache ==================================================
   341	
   342	    /**
   343	     * @brief Per-thread cache state for geometric batch growth.
   344	     *
   345	     * Each thread that interacts with the pool maintains one of these
   346	     * structures in thread-local storage. The local free list uses the
   347	     * same embedded next-pointer scheme as the shared free list but
   348	     * requires no atomic operations since only the owning thread touches it.
   349	     */
   350	    struct ThreadCache
   351	    {
   352	        void* free_list_head;           ///< Head of the thread-local free block chain.
   353	        std::size_t cached_count;       ///< Number of blocks currently in the local cache.
   354	        std::size_t current_batch_size; ///< Batch size for the next trip to the shared pool.
   355	    };
   356	
   357	    /**
   358	     * @brief Retrieves or initializes the calling thread's cache.
   359	     */
   360	    ThreadCache& thread_cache();
   361	
   362	
   363	    // === Member State ========================================================
   364	
   365	    // -- Free list (shared, contended) --
   366	    std::atomic<TaggedPointer> free_list_head_;  ///< ABA-safe head of the embedded free list.
   367	
   368	    // -- Pool geometry (constant after construction) --
   369	    std::size_t block_size_;            ///< Effective block size (aligned, >= sizeof(void*)).
   370	    std::size_t block_alignment_;       ///< Alignment guarantee for block starting addresses.
   371	    std::size_t chunk_size_;            ///< Size of each OS-acquired chunk in bytes.
   372	    std::size_t blocks_per_chunk_;      ///< Number of blocks carved from each chunk.
   373	    std::size_t budget_ceiling_;        ///< Maximum total bytes acquirable from the OS.
   374	
   375	    // -- Chunk tracking (grows monotonically, never shrinks) --
   376	    ChunkDescriptor* chunk_descriptors_;  ///< Fixed array of chunk descriptors.
   377	    std::size_t chunk_count_;             ///< Number of chunks currently acquired.
   378	    std::size_t max_chunk_count_;         ///< Capacity of the chunk descriptor array.
   379

   381	    std::size_t initial_thread_batch_;  ///< Starting batch size for geometric growth.
   382	    std::size_t max_thread_batch_;      ///< Maximum batch size cap per thread.

   386	        std::atomic<TaggedPointer>::is_always_lock_free,
   387	        "ProcessMemoryPool requires lock-free 16-byte atomics. "

{"language": "cpp", "code": "/**
 * @file ProcessMemoryPool.hpp
 * @brief Process-wide fixed-size block pool with lock-free allocation.
 *
 * ProcessMemoryPool is the mechanical core of Chevron's memory hierarchy.
 * It acquires large chunks of memory from the operating system, carves them
 * into fixed-size blocks, and distributes those blocks to downstream
 * components through a lock-free embedded free list.
 *
 * This class is not used directly by downstream consumers. It is composed
 * as a value member inside MemoryCore, which provides the policy surface
 * (budget enforcement, preallocation, acquire/release interface) on top of
 * the pool's mechanical operations.
 *
 * @note Thread-safe. All allocation and deallocation operations are lock-free.
 *
 * Chevron Library — Internal Infrastructure
 */

#ifndef CHEVRON_MEMORY_PROCESS_MEMORY_POOL_HPP
#define CHEVRON_MEMORY_PROCESS_MEMORY_POOL_HPP

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

namespace chevron::memory {

// ============================================================================
// Supporting Types
// ============================================================================

/**
 * @brief Lightweight value type describing a contiguous region of memory.
 *
 * Carries a base pointer and byte size. Does not own the memory it describes.
 * Used as the currency for memory transfer between hierarchy components.
 */
struct MemoryRegion
{
    void* base;         ///< Starting address of the region.
    std::size_t size;   ///< Size of the region in bytes.
};


/**
 * @brief Descriptor for a single acquired chunk of OS memory.
 *
 * Stored in the pool's chunk descriptor array. Records the base address
 * and size of each chunk so that all chunks can be released back to the
 * OS at pool destruction.
 */
struct ChunkDescriptor
{
    void* base;         ///< Starting address returned by the OS allocation call.
    std::size_t size;   ///< Size of the chunk in bytes.
};


/**
 * @brief Tagged pointer for ABA-safe lock-free operations on the free list.
 *
 * Pairs a block pointer with a monotonically increasing generation counter.
 * The counter increments on every push or pop, ensuring that a CAS operation
 * detects any intervening modifications even if the pointer value returns to
 * a previously observed state.
 *
 * @note This type must be 16 bytes and lock-free under std::atomic to
 *       guarantee the pool's lock-free contract. A static assertion in
 *       ProcessMemoryPool enforces this at compile time.
 */
struct TaggedPointer
{
    void* ptr;                  ///< Pointer to a free block (or nullptr if list is empty).
    std::uint64_t generation;   ///< Monotonically increasing operation counter.
};


/**
 * @brief Construction parameters for ProcessMemoryPool.
 *
 * Bundles all construction-time configuration into a single value type,
 * keeping the constructor signature clean and self-documenting.
 */
struct PoolConfig
{
    std::size_t block_size;             ///< Size of each block in bytes (before alignment adjustment).
    std::size_t block_alignment;        ///< Alignment guarantee for every block's starting address.
    std::size_t chunk_size;             ///< Size of each OS-acquired chunk in bytes.
    std::size_t budget_ceiling;         ///< Maximum total bytes the pool may acquire from the OS.
    std::size_t initial_thread_batch;   ///< Starting batch size for thread-local geometric growth.
    std::size_t max_thread_batch;       ///< Maximum batch size a thread may claim in one trip.
};


// ============================================================================
// ProcessMemoryPool
// ============================================================================

/**
 * @class ProcessMemoryPool
 * @brief Lock-free fixed-size block pool with embedded free list and
 *        per-thread geometric caching.
 *
 * ## Mechanical Overview
 *
 * The pool acquires large contiguous chunks from the OS via aligned
 * allocation and carves each chunk into fixed-size blocks. Free blocks
 * are linked together through an embedded singly-linked list — each free
 * block stores a pointer to the next free block in its own memory. The
 * list head is an atomic tagged pointer (pointer + generation counter)
 * that supports ABA-safe compare-and-swap for lock-free push and pop.
 *
 * ## Thread-Local Caching
 *
 * To reduce contention on the shared free list, each thread maintains a
 * private cache of blocks. When the cache is empty, the thread acquires
 * a batch from the shared list. The batch size starts at a configured
 * initial value and doubles on each subsequent trip (geometric growth),
 * up to a configured maximum. This keeps high-demand threads away from
 * the shared atomics on the common allocation path.
 *
 * ## Growth Model
 *
 * The pool starts empty and acquires chunks lazily as demand requires,
 * up to the configured budget ceiling. Once the ceiling is reached,
 * further growth requests result in std::bad_alloc. Chunks are never
 * returned to the OS during runtime — all OS-level deallocation occurs
 * at pool destruction.
 *
 * ## Ownership
 *
 * ProcessMemoryPool is composed inside MemoryCore as a value member.
 * It is not intended for direct use by downstream consumers.
 */
class ProcessMemoryPool
{
public:
    // === Lifecycle ===========================================================

    /**
     * @brief Constructs the pool with the given configuration.
     *
     * Validates and adjusts configuration parameters:
     * - block_size is rounded up to the nearest multiple of block_alignment.
     * - block_size is enforced to be at least sizeof(void*).
     * - chunk_size is rounded up to the nearest multiple of effective block_size.
     * - max_chunk_count is derived from budget_ceiling / chunk_size.
     * - The chunk descriptor array is allocated to hold max_chunk_count entries.
     *
     * No OS memory is acquired for blocks at this point. The pool starts
     * with an empty free list and zero chunks. Use preallocate() to
     * acquire initial chunks before the pool enters active use.
     *
     * @param config Construction-time configuration parameters.
     *
     * @throws std::invalid_argument if block_size is zero, chunk_size is zero,
     *         budget_ceiling is zero, or budget_ceiling < chunk_size.
     */
    explicit ProcessMemoryPool(const PoolConfig& config);

    /**
     * @brief Destroys the pool and releases all chunks back to the OS.
     *
     * All chunks tracked in the descriptor array are released. Thread-local
     * caches are not drained — their blocks reside within chunks that are
     * being released as whole units, so individual block cleanup is unnecessary.
     */
    ~ProcessMemoryPool();

    ProcessMemoryPool(const ProcessMemoryPool&) = delete;
    ProcessMemoryPool& operator=(const ProcessMemoryPool&) = delete;
    ProcessMemoryPool(ProcessMemoryPool&&) = delete;
    ProcessMemoryPool& operator=(ProcessMemoryPool&&) = delete;


    // === Core Operations =====================================================

    /**
     * @brief Acquires a single block from the pool.
     *
     * Attempts to pop a block from the calling thread's local cache first.
     * If the local cache is empty, acquires a batch from the shared free
     * list (triggering chunk growth if the shared list is also exhausted)
     * and refills the local cache before returning a block.
     *
     * @return Pointer to the acquired block, aligned to block_alignment.
     *
     * @throws std::bad_alloc if the pool is exhausted (budget ceiling reached
     *         and all blocks are allocated).
     */
    [[nodiscard]] void* allocate();

    /**
     * @brief Returns a single block to the pool.
     *
     * Pushes the block onto the calling thread's local cache. If the local
     * cache exceeds a drain threshold, a batch is returned to the shared
     * free list to make blocks available to other threads.
     *
     * @param block Pointer to the block being returned. Must have been
     *              obtained from this pool's allocate(). Passing a pointer
     *              not obtained from this pool is undefined behavior.
     */
    void deallocate(void* block) noexcept;

    /**
     * @brief Acquires one or more chunks from the OS to prepopulate the pool.
     *
     * Each acquired chunk is carved into blocks and threaded into the shared
     * free list. Intended to be called during initialization before the pool
     * enters active concurrent use, avoiding growth-path synchronization
     * during runtime.
     *
     * @param chunk_count Number of chunks to acquire.
     *
     * @throws std::bad_alloc if acquiring the requested chunks would exceed
     *         the budget ceiling.
     */
    void preallocate(std::size_t chunk_count);


    // === Diagnostics =========================================================

    /**
     * @brief Returns the effective block size after alignment adjustment.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t effective_block_size() const noexcept;

    /**
     * @brief Returns the block alignment guarantee.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t alignment() const noexcept;

    /**
     * @brief Returns the number of chunks currently acquired from the OS.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t acquired_chunk_count() const noexcept;

    /**
     * @brief Returns the maximum number of chunks the pool may acquire.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t max_chunks() const noexcept;

    /**
     * @brief Returns the total number of blocks across all acquired chunks.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::size_t total_block_count() const noexcept;

    /**
     * @brief Returns the current generation counter from the free list head.
     *
     * This counter increments on every push and pop operation against the
     * shared free list. It serves primarily as the ABA guard but also
     * provides a total operation count for diagnostics.
     */
    [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t generation() const noexcept;


private:
    // === Internal Operations =================================================

    /**
     * @brief Acquires a new chunk from the OS and integrates it into the pool.
     *
     * Allocates aligned memory, records the chunk in the descriptor array,
     * carves the chunk into blocks, and threads those blocks into the shared
     * free list.
     *
     * @throws std::bad_alloc if the budget ceiling would be exceeded or if
     *         the OS allocation fails.
     */
    void grow();

    /**
     * @brief Carves a raw chunk into blocks and threads them into the free list.
     *
     * Walks the chunk from base to end, writing embedded next-pointers into
     * each block to form a singly-linked chain of free blocks. The chain is
     * then prepended to the shared free list via CAS.
     *
     * @param chunk_base Starting address of the chunk (must be aligned).
     * @param chunk_size Size of the chunk in bytes.
     */
    void carve_and_thread(void* chunk_base, std::size_t chunk_size);

    /**
     * @brief Pops a batch of blocks from the shared free list into a
     *        thread-local cache.
     *
     * Walks the free list to find the Nth block, then CAS-swaps the head
     * to the block after the Nth, detaching the entire batch in a single
     * atomic operation. Retries on CAS failure.
     *
     * @param batch_size Number of blocks to pop.
     * @return Pointer to the head of the detached chain, or nullptr if
     *         insufficient blocks are available.
     */
    void* pop_batch(std::size_t batch_size);

    /**
     * @brief Pushes a chain of blocks from a thread-local cache back onto
     *        the shared free list.
     *
     * Links the chain's tail to the current head and CAS-swaps the head
     * to the chain's first block, prepending the entire batch in a single
     * atomic operation. Retries on CAS failure.
     *
     * @param head Pointer to the first block in the chain.
     * @param tail Pointer to the last block in the chain.
     */
    void push_batch(void* head, void* tail);

    /**
     * @brief Platform-specific aligned memory acquisition from the OS.
     *
     * Acquires a contiguous region of at least the requested size with
     * the specified alignment. The returned pointer must be freed with
     * release_to_os().
     *
     * @param size Number of bytes to acquire.
     * @param alignment Required alignment of the returned address.
     * @return Pointer to the acquired region.
     *
     * @throws std::bad_alloc if the OS refuses the allocation.
     */
    static void* acquire_from_os(std::size_t size, std::size_t alignment);

    /**
     * @brief Platform-specific memory release back to the OS.
     *
     * Releases a region previously acquired by acquire_from_os().
     *
     * @param base Starting address of the region.
     * @param size Size of the region in bytes.
     */
    static void release_to_os(void* base, std::size_t size) noexcept;


    // === Thread-Local Cache ==================================================

    /**
     * @brief Per-thread cache state for geometric batch growth.
     *
     * Each thread that interacts with the pool maintains one of these
     * structures in thread-local storage. The local free list uses the
     * same embedded next-pointer scheme as the shared free list but
     * requires no atomic operations since only the owning thread touches it.
     */
    struct ThreadCache
    {
        void* free_list_head;           ///< Head of the thread-local free block chain.
        std::size_t cached_count;       ///< Number of blocks currently in the local cache.
        std::size_t current_batch_size; ///< Batch size for the next trip to the shared pool.
    };

    /**
     * @brief Retrieves or initializes the calling thread's cache.
     */
    ThreadCache& thread_cache();


    // === Member State ========================================================

    // -- Free list (shared, contended) --
    std::atomic<TaggedPointer> free_list_head_;  ///< ABA-safe head of the embedded free list.

    // -- Pool geometry (constant after construction) --
    std::size_t block_size_;            ///< Effective block size (aligned, >= sizeof(void*)).
    std::size_t block_alignment_;       ///< Alignment guarantee for block starting addresses.
    std::size_t chunk_size_;            ///< Size of each OS-acquired chunk in bytes.
    std::size_t blocks_per_chunk_;      ///< Number of blocks carved from each chunk.
    std::size_t budget_ceiling_;        ///< Maximum total bytes acquirable from the OS.

    // -- Chunk tracking (grows monotonically, never shrinks) --
    ChunkDescriptor* chunk_descriptors_;  ///< Fixed array of chunk descriptors.
    std::size_t chunk_count_;             ///< Number of chunks currently acquired.
    std::size_t max_chunk_count_;         ///< Capacity of the chunk descriptor array.

    // -- Thread-local cache parameters (constant after construction) --
    std::size_t initial_thread_batch_;  ///< Starting batch size for geometric growth.
    std::size_t max_thread_batch_;      ///< Maximum batch size cap per thread.

    // -- Compile-time guarantees --
    static_assert(
        std::atomic<TaggedPointer>::is_always_lock_free,
        "ProcessMemoryPool requires lock-free 16-byte atomics. "
        "The target platform does not support lock-free std::atomic<TaggedPointer>."
    );
};

} // namespace chevron::memory

#endif // CHEVRON_MEMORY_PROCESS_MEMORY_POOL_HPP

        "The target platform does not support lock-free std::atomic<TaggedPointer>."
    );

chat_messages.text:
That's an important question. Let me walk through exactly what happens.

---

**When a thread dies, its `thread_local` variables are destroyed.**

This is defined behavior in the C++ standard. When a thread exits — whether normally, via exception, or through any other termination path — all of its `thread_local` objects are destroyed in the reverse order of their construction. So when your thread pool catches an unhandled exception and the thread joins, that thread's `ThreadCache` is destroyed. Its destructor runs (or in this case, since it's a plain struct with no destructor, its storage is simply reclaimed).

**What's in that cache when it dies?**

The `ThreadCache` holds a local free list — a chain of blocks that were popped from the shared pool but haven't been used or returned yet. When the thread dies and the `ThreadCache` is destroyed, those block pointers are gone. The blocks themselves still exist — they're inside chunks that the pool owns — but nobody holds a reference to them anymore. They're not in the shared free list (they were popped out), and they're not in any thread's local cache (the owning thread is dead). They're orphaned.

**This is a memory leak within the pool.**

Not a leak to the OS — the chunks are still tracked in the chunk descriptor array and will be released at pool destruction. But those orphaned blocks are unavailable for allocation for the remainder of the pool's lifetime. They're effectively dead space. The pool's budget ceiling accounts for them as acquired memory, but they can never be handed out again because no free list — shared or local — contains them.

**How big is the problem?**

It depends on how many blocks are in the dead thread's cache at the time of death. If the thread had just refilled with a geometrically grown batch — say 64 blocks — those 64 blocks are gone. If your block size is 64KB, that's 4MB of pool memory permanently unavailable. If threads die frequently (which in a well-designed thread pool they shouldn't, but you said you can't predict user code), the leakage compounds.

**The fix**

The `ThreadCache` needs a destructor that returns its cached blocks to the shared free list before the thread exits. Since `ThreadCache` is currently a plain struct, you'd either give it a destructor that calls `push_batch` on the pool, or wrap it in a type that handles cleanup.

The challenge is that the `ThreadCache` as a `thread_local` static inside `thread_cache()` doesn't have a reference back to the pool — it doesn't know which pool to return blocks to. You'd need to give it one. This means the `ThreadCache` struct grows to include a pointer to the owning `ProcessMemoryPool` instance, set on first access. The destructor uses that pointer to push any remaining cached blocks back to the shared free list.

There's a subtlety here with destruction ordering. If the pool itself is being destroyed at the same time threads are dying (process shutdown), the `ThreadCache` destructor might try to push blocks onto a pool that's already been destroyed or is mid-destruction. This is the classic `thread_local` destruction order problem. In your case, this is handled by your systematic teardown — the thread pool joins all threads before `AppProcess` destroys `MemoryCore` which destroys the pool. So by the time the pool's destructor runs, all threads have already joined and their `ThreadCache` destructors have already run. The ordering is safe as long as your teardown sequence is respected.

For the mid-runtime case — a thread dying unexpectedly while the pool is still alive and healthy — the `ThreadCache` destructor safely pushes blocks back to the shared free list via `push_batch`, which is a CAS operation that works from any thread, including a dying one (the destructor runs while the thread still exists, just before its storage is reclaimed).

**No undefined behavior, no OS-level leak — but a real pool-internal leak without the fix.**

So the `ThreadCache` struct needs to become something like:

```
struct ThreadCache
{
    void* free_list_head;
    std::size_t cached_count;
    std::size_t current_batch_size;
    ProcessMemoryPool* owner;

    ~ThreadCache();  // Returns cached blocks to owner->push_batch()
};
```

The destructor drains the local free list back to the shared pool. The `owner` pointer is set once on first access and never changes.
